inlines.v: DECE'ASE, noun [Latin to depart or to withdraw.] Literally, departure; hence, departure from this life; death; applied to human beings only. Moses and Elias, who appeared in glory, and spoke of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem. Luke 9:31. DECE'ASE, verb intransitive To depart from this life; to die. Gen. Washington deceased, December 14, 1799, in the 68th year of his age.
